advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Iterate mount-point arguments via a positional-array / `"$@"` instead of the unquoted `$targets` string in check-mounts.sh.
evidence: Current mount points (/var/gerrit, /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch) contain no spaces, so this is latent rather than currently triggered.
advisory.finding: check-mounts.sh builds its target list with unquoted word-splitting (`targets="$*"` then `for mount_point in $targets`), so a mount-point argument containing whitespace is split into multiple bogus targets and a glob metacharacter would be expanded against the CWD.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fall back to a placeholder (e.g. `?`) when describe_source yields no source in check-mounts.sh's OK line.
evidence: infra/scripts/check-mounts.sh:42-47: describe_source can produce empty output if neither findmnt nor /proc/mounts yields a source
advisory.finding: In check-mounts.sh the OK line prints `describe_source` output that can be empty (findmnt exits 1 for an unusual mount and the /proc/mounts awk prints nothing), yielding an `OK <mp> <- ` line with a blank source that reads as a partial/failed lookup even though the mount is confirmed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the chmod-order source-index test with an observable-behavior assertion (e.g. execute the block against a fixture and assert the directory mode is 0700 before/at the point the markers are written), or acknowledge it as an intentional structural pin.
evidence: assert chmod_at < required_at and chmod_at < proof_at
docstring concedes: "Both orders behave identically under root, so there is no observable difference to assert on"

Litmus (Rule 4): renaming the variable or reformatting the three lines would break this test with no behavior change — a change-detector against SOURCE CODE UNDER TEST (user_data.sh is the unit under test)
advisory.finding: test_the_scratch_mount_is_tightened_before_the_markers_are_written asserts on the SOURCE TEXT of user_data.sh (str.index of literal code fragments) rather than observable behavior, so it is a source-grep/change-detector: it breaks on any behavior-preserving refactor (renaming $GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT, reformatting, or extracting the chmod/touch block into a helper) even though nothing about the mount-point permissions changed.
scenarios: A future refactor reformats or renames the chmod/marker block; the test fails despite identical permission behavior.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a check-mounts.sh test that removes `mountpoint`/`findmnt` from PATH and provides a fake /proc/mounts so the awk fallback branch is exercised for both the mounted and plain-directory cases.
evidence: infra/scripts/check-mounts.sh is_mounted fallback: awk -v mp="$1" '$2 == mp { found = 1 } END { exit found ? 0 : 1 }' /proc/mounts
test stubs always provide mountpoint: _stub(fake_bin / "mountpoint", "exit 1\n") and _stub(fake_bin / "mountpoint", "exit 0\n")

Named violating input: on a host where `command -v mountpoint` fails, is_mounted() falls through to `awk ... /proc/mounts`; no test removes mountpoint from PATH to drive that branch, so a defect in the awk fallback (e.g. wrong field index) would ship undetected
This is newly introduced behavior — the entire check-mounts.sh file is added (+) in this diff
advisory.finding: The check-mounts.sh fallback paths for a host without util-linux (the `awk ... /proc/mounts` branch in is_mounted() and the awk fallback in describe_source()) are never executed by any test: every check-mounts test stubs `mountpoint` (and `findmnt`) on PATH, so `command -v mountpoint` always succeeds and the /proc/mounts fallback — a newly-added code path — is untested.
scenarios: Operator runs check-mounts.sh mid-incident on a minimal/rescue host lacking util-linux mountpoint; the untested /proc/mounts fallback determines pass/fail.
